// Fixture for scripts/test-scripts.sh (wallclock-check): stored as .txt so the tree's
// tools never compile it. Every case below is allowed, each for its own reason.
import { screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

it("keeps what it can say a reason for", async () => {
  // wall-clock: the test measures how a real timer paces a retry, so the clock must follow real time
  vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true });
  await screen.findByText("x", {}, { timeout: 500 }); // wall-clock: the element is absent after 500 ms by design; a longer wait only delays the pass
});

it("uses what is generous", async () => {
  await screen.findByText("y", {}, { timeout: 30_000 });
  await waitFor(() => expect(1).toBe(1), { timeout: 45000 });
  await vi.waitFor(() => expect(2).toBe(2), { timeout: 30_000 });
  await vi.waitFor(
    () => {
      expect(3).toBe(3);
    },
    { timeout: 30_000, interval: 10 },
  );
  // vi.waitFor( named in a comment is not a call
}, 60_000);

it("takes a request field named timeout", async () => {
  const body = {
    timeout: 30, // wall-clock: request body field, not a wait
  };
  expect(body).toBeTruthy();
});
